biggestGap: The play camera crops White's own back rank off the bottom of the frame. All eight rank-1 square centres project 20-23 px BELOW the canvas edge (g1 at y=649, canvas ends y=628), leaving only a 22-28 px sliver of each square inside the picture. Aiming at where e1 or g1 actually looks like it is puts the click on black page background and nothing happens; the move only lands if you click the top sliver instead. This is deterministic at every window size (1280x720, 1280x640, 1600x900 all identical, because interactive.ts forces the canvas to a 2.39:1 letterbox), and it bites on move 2, when most people move a knight.
critiqueDetail:
It genuinely plays. I drove the real canvas with my own Playwright script in interactive mode, projecting squares through window.__WC__.world.camera and clicking with page.mouse, and completed an 11-move game: 1.e4 Nc6 2.Nf3 e6 3.Bc4 d5 4.d3 dxc4 5.Nc3 cxd3 6.O-O Nb4 7.Bg5 f6 8.Nd5 exd5 9.Qxd3 Nxd3 10.cxd3 fxg5 11.Nxg5 Qxg5. Castling worked. Nine captures happened. Every single position was replayed through a fresh Engine instance loaded from /src/chess/index.ts and every one was legal with an exact FEN round-trip; result stayed 'playing', the rAF loop never stopped, and there were zero page errors and zero console errors across the whole game. A second 10-move game (a3 Nc6 d4 Nf6 c4 Bd6 b3 O-O e3 a6 g4 Nxg4 h4 b6 a4 Qf6 b4 Nxb4 c5 Bxc5) did the same. tools/play-test.mjs also passes on its own: e2-e4 accepted, engine answered Nc6, no errors.

Abuse did not break it. Clicking an empty square, clicking the engine's own rook on a8, clicking the same pawn twice, clicking 5,5 far off the board, clicking a2 then h6 as an illegal destination, and clicking a square while state.thinking was true all left the FEN byte-identical and the turn unchanged. Selection is a ray-plane hit test against y=0, so an off-board click simply returns null and clears the selection.

The framing is the fault. PLAY_SHOT in src/core/shots.ts promises 'the whole board inside the frame with margin'. It is not. src/game/interactive.ts fitCanvas() overrides main.ts's fit() and pins camera.aspect to RENDER.aspect (2.388) and the canvas to width x width/2.388, so interactive play is always the cinema letterbox, and from eye [0,15,-21] with fov 30 the near rank falls out of the bottom. I measured the clickable band of every square down the d-file: d2 is 81 px tall, d3 68, d4 57 ... and d1 is 25 px, with its centre 20 px outside the picture. Rank 1 moves DO work if you deliberately click that sliver: I played Nf3 six times out of six from the start position that way. But my first, naive harness -- which aims at the square centre the way a person does -- could not play move 2 at all and reported 'SQUARE OFF SCREEN'. That is exactly the experience a human gets.

Second finding, nearly as bad: the engine's answer decays as wreckage accumulates. Real seconds from my move landing to the engine's move landing, across the 11-move game: 1.14, 0.98, 0.97, 0.81, 3.99, 3.95, 3.87, 3.72, 36.46, 30.39, 28.87. It tracks scene mesh count exactly (339 -> 396 -> 471 -> 494 as debris piles up). The chess is not the cost: the same 60,000-node search run synchronously in the page took 660 ms cold and 232 ms warm. This is renderer starvation, and the caveat is real -- this box runs SwiftShader at 0.239 fps (3,927 ms per frame) with the adaptive scaler already at its lowest rung (512 px buffer behind a 1280 px CSS width), so a GPU would be far kinder. But the shape of it -- the game gets slower the longer you play, precisely as it gets interesting -- is a design coupling, not just slow hardware.

Captures do resolve correctly: the victim disappears, mesh count grows by 55-75 per shatter, and rubble is visibly strewn across the marble in the final screenshot. It arrives late, though -- debris was not yet in the scene graph 2.5 s of wall clock after the blade landed, because the spawn is scheduled on world.time, which at 0.24 fps runs about 80x behind the wall clock. The same clamped clock leaves capture flares blooming at full brightness long after the strike, and by move 12 the centre of the board is a white smear you cannot read pieces through.

One stability note: the page lost window.__WC__ twice, both times only in stress scripts that called game.setPosition() repeatedly between shatters. Eleven moves of ordinary play never came close to it.

The scripted path is NOT regressed. Two king-surrender captures at t=2.8 are byte-identical (md5 45ebe28f78b6837bb2816b5fcccbe9ab, 2,264,723 bytes each), and tools/verify-mate.mjs reports all three lines ending in a real verified checkmate: wreckage 21 plies / 9 captures / Qxc8#, strike 7 plies / Qxf7#, scholar 7 plies / Qxf7#, each with inCheck=true and legalReplies=0.
metrics: 11 full moves played through the canvas, all positions legal + FEN round-trip exact, 0 page errors. Engine reply (real s): 1.14, 0.98, 0.97, 0.81, 3.99, 3.95, 3.87, 3.72, 36.46, 30.39, 28.87. Click-to-accept 0.23-0.27 s throughout. Renderer 0.239 fps / 3927 ms per frame, buffer 512 px behind 1280 px CSS. 60k-node search in-page: 660 ms cold, 232 ms warm. Scene meshes 339 -> 494 over 9 captures. Rank-1 clickable band 22-28 px, square centres 20-23 px below the canvas edge; identical at 1280x720, 1280x640, 1600x900. Back-rank Nf3 6/6 when clicking the sliver. Scripted: cmp byte-identical (md5 45ebe28f78b6837bb2816b5fcccbe9ab); verify-mate 3/3 real checkmates, 0 legal replies each.

history.gap: none — 3/3 demo lines verified as real checkmate with zero legal replies

The play camera crops White's own back rank off the bottom of the frame — all eight rank-1 square centres sit 20-23 px below the canvas edge, leaving a 22-28 px sliver, so clicking where your own knight or king appears to be does nothing. Deterministic at every window size, and it hits on move 2.
